Hi, 
I have the same problem using this HLS playlist:
https://devimages.apple.com.edgekey.net/streaming/examples/bipbop_4x3/bipbop_4x3_variant.m3u8
(my initial observations was posted here: #150)
- It works fine on Emulator Nexus 5 x86 (1,5Go RAM) - API 23
- It fails after one or two segments on the same Emulator with API 16 or 17
  
  I also tried another homemade HLS stream and what i conclude is that
  on API 23 i can read all variant quality stream, but on API 16 or 17 it will works fine as long as i stay on the lower quality/bitrate and fail as soon as i hit a better quality: so it's related to the stream bitrate.

Problem is that by better quality i'm talking about 2/3 MBs which is not much.

It seems that the player starts with the poorest quality and then try to go on the better one if the bandwith allows it. It would help if at this point, the better quality is just refused if the device cannot handle it instead of throwing this Exception so the device can continue to play on the lower quality.

No need to detect that from the playlist (the info is not allways provided), it should happen on the quality switch process, which should be prevented if the better quality is actually not playable.

That will not solve the case where no variant are playable, but it would help in most case, and it will follow the "adaptative streaming" philosophy.

What do you think ?

EDIT: answered here: #150

Best,
Thomas

For the Acer device at least, this issue can be resolved by explicitly setting a minimum input size in the format used to configure the decoder. We'll merge a change that does this shortly. I have no idea whether this also resolves the issue on other devices. My guess would be that it probably does for physical devices. For the emulator, I'm not so sure.
